children.title: Trump names Michael Ellis CIA deputy director
children.description_medium: On February 3, 2025, President Donald Trump named Michael Ellis as deputy director of the CIA. Ellis, a lawyer and former aide to Representative Devin Nunes, was sworn in on February 10. The deputy director role does not require Senate confirmation. His title was deputy director.
children.description_long: President Donald Trump named Michael Ellis as deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency on February 3, 2025. The Washington Post reported that Ellis was a lawyer and former aide to Representative Devin Nunes, and noted that the deputy director position does not require Senate confirmation. The CIA later announced that Ellis was sworn in on February 10. These two supplied sources document the appointment and the subsequent oath of office, so the event chronology includes both dates while distinguishing the announcement from the swearing-in. Ellis had previously served as NSA general counsel and as a senior director for intelligence programs at the National Security Council, according to the appointment report. The available sources support describing his professional background and his appointment to a senior agency role. The “political ally” characterization appears in the reported context, but the sources do not establish that political loyalty rather than professional qualifications determined the selection. This record therefore states the documented appointment and background without asserting that the selection was improper or based solely on allegiance.
children.date_uncertainty: February 3 is the appointment announcement date; the CIA says Ellis was sworn in February 10, 2025.

children.title: Gabbard revokes clearances of 37 intelligence officials
children.description_medium: On August 19, 2025, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearances of 37 current and former intelligence officials. The Washington Post reported the action as a separate August event, distinct from earlier CIA and National Intelligence Council personnel changes. The clearance action was its own decision.
children.description_long: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearances of 37 current and former intelligence officials, according to Washington Post reporting published August 19, 2025. The packet identifies this as a discrete action, separate from the appointment of Michael Ellis, the March probationary CIA dismissals and the May National Intelligence Council personnel changes. The supplied report supports the number of people whose clearances were revoked and the date of the announcement. It does not establish that the action formed part of a single personnel campaign spanning every agency or specialist category described in the original omnibus account. The source also does not establish the broad asserted motive that intelligence specialists were replaced by loyalists chosen through social-media activism. This event should therefore be represented as the clearance action reported by the newspaper, with its own date and institutional scope. The broader cumulative-purge narrative remains unsupported by the specific source record supplied for this task.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the Washington Post publication and reported announcement date.

children.title: CIA removes senior Russia expert days after Alaska summit
children.description_medium: The Washington Post reported on August 27, 2025, that the Trump administration had removed the CIA’s senior-most Russia expert days after the Alaska summit. This personnel action was separately reported from Gabbard’s August 19 revocation of 37 intelligence officials’ clearances. The report tied its timing to that summit.
children.description_long: The Washington Post reported on August 27, 2025, that the Trump administration had removed the CIA’s senior-most Russia expert days after the Alaska summit. The report treats the removal as a distinct personnel action in the intelligence community. It is separate from the August 19 announcement that Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearances of 37 current and former officials, even though both events appeared in reporting about changes affecting intelligence personnel. The supplied source supports the timing relative to the summit and the reported removal of the CIA official described as its senior-most Russia expert. It does not by itself establish that this removal was caused by the clearance action, that a single Washington Post investigation documented a combined purge across several agencies, or that the official was replaced by a political loyalist. The event is therefore limited to the reported removal and its chronology. Broader claims about the cumulative effect and motive require separate evidence beyond the source supplied here.
children.date_uncertainty: August 27 is the article publication date; the report dates the removal as occurring days after the Alaska summit.
